seoTitle: Macro Calculator - Find Your Ideal Macros
metaDescription: Free online Macro Calculator. Find the perfect balance of Protein, Carbs, and Fats tailored to your specific fitness goals, diet type, and body weight.
intro: Counting calories isn't enough to change your body composition. Our free Macro Calculator breaks down your daily calories into the optimal grams of Protein, Carbohydrates, and Fats for your goals.
whatIs: The Macro (Macronutrient) Calculator is an advanced nutritional planning tool. It takes your total daily calorie target and divides it into specific grammatical targets for the three main food groups needed by the body: proteins, fats, and carbs.
howToUse: Enter your physical stats (age, weight, height, activity level).
Select your goal (lose weight, maintain, build muscle).
Select a preferred diet style (Balanced, Low Carb, High Protein, Keto).
The tool outputs exactly how many grams of each macro you should eat daily.
howItWorks: The tool first calculates your daily calorie goal. It then applies specific mathematical ratios based on your diet type. It knows that 1 gram of protein = 4 calories, 1 gram of carbs = 4 calories, and 1 gram of fat = 9 calories, dividing the totals accordingly.
workedExample: Goal: 2000 calories on a Balanced diet (30% Protein, 35% Fat, 35% Carbs). Protein: 600 cals / 4 = 150g. Fat: 700 cals / 9 = 78g. Carbs: 700 cals / 4 = 175g.
resultInterpretation: The generated numbers dictate exactly what your daily meals should consist of. Hitting your protein target preserves muscle, fats regulate hormones, and carbs provide energy.
useCases: Body Recomposition: Eating a high-protein, maintenance-calorie macro split to lose fat and build muscle simultaneously.
Keto Dieting: Calculating a strict low-carb (under 5%), high-fat macro split to ensure the body enters ketosis.
Athletic Performance: Generating a high-carb macro profile to fuel marathon training or intense endurance sports.
tipsAndLimitations: Protein is the most important macro to hit accurately, especially if you are in a caloric deficit, to prevent muscle wasting.
Alcohol is technically a fourth 'macro' (7 calories per gram) but provides no nutritional value and is not included in standard macro planning.

faq.question: Can I eat whatever I want as long as it fits my macros (IIFYM)?
faq.answer: Technically, yes. For pure weight loss/gain, the source of the macros doesn't matter. However, for overall health, digestion, and micronutrients (vitamins), you should get your macros from whole, unprocessed foods.

faq.question: What if I miss my fat and carb targets?
faq.answer: As long as you hit your total calorie goal and your protein goal, the exact ratio of carbs to fats is mostly personal preference and will not severely impact your progress.

disclaimer: Macro ratios provided are general recommendations. Individuals with specific medical conditions (like diabetes or kidney issues) should consult a physician before significantly altering their diet.
